title: Lack of clarity on how unloading works recursively
body:
In [prompt to unload](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#prompt-to-unload-a-document) and [unload](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#unload-a-document), the algorithms recursively call itself on the Document's [list of the descendant browsing contexts](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#list-of-the-descendant-browsing-contexts). However, a few questions spring out of the liveliness of the list: is it a copy of the list, or is it a reference?

**What happens if a nested browsing context is added when this algorithm is in the recursion step?** It seems like implementations skip that newly added browsing context, which suggests that the list is copied.

**What happens if a nested browsing context is removed when this algorithm is in the recursion step?** This case is a bit more complicated. Despite the fact that the [spec](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#the-iframe-element) says

> When an `iframe` element is removed from a document, the user agent must discard the element's nested browsing context, if it is not null, and then set the element's nested browsing context to null.
>
> Note: This happens without any `unload` events firing (the nested browsing context and its `Document` are discarded, not unloaded).

It seems like many implementations (I tested Chrome, Safari, and Firefox) do fire `pagehide` and `unload` events when the `iframe` is removed (but not `beforeunload`).

Back to the original issue though. Even if the list of descendants is copied, I don't expect `pagehide` and `unload` events to be fired in the original unload algorithm, after the iframe removal is done. They have the [page showing](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#page-showing) and [fired unload](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#fired-unload) flags to prevent firing those events twice. So the copy hypothesis works okay here.

On the other hand, it is a problem for `beforeunload`: it doesn't seem like implementations actually fire `beforeunload` for browsing contexts removed when the algorithm is running. This implies that implementations have some sort of liveliness measure that prevents them from firing `beforeunload` even when the prompt to unload has been running.

In [Blink's case](https://cs.chromium.org/chromium/src/third_party/blink/renderer/core/loader/frame_loader.cc?l=1449-1479&rcl=7aaa0d3df4a9d7d7c24b8f20d8362e76e1569e16), they get a copy of the descendants when firing `beforeunload`, and when iteration through the list they check if that browsing context is still [in the document](https://cs.chromium.org/chromium/src/third_party/blink/renderer/core/loader/frame_loader.cc?l=1468-1469&rcl=7aaa0d3df4a9d7d7c24b8f20d8362e76e1569e16).

Tests I used are available at https://github.com/TimothyGu/document-open-tests, files with names starting with `unload-event-frame-`.

----

As it is right now, the recursion is sort of atypical in that it gets all the browsing contexts using tree order traversal in the top level call of the algorithm, and that list is then iterated through. In other words, the recursion only happens for at most one level. This has impacts on the [ignore-opens-during-unload counter](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#ignore-opens-during-unload-counter).

Imagine a nesting A → B → C.

- If I were to unload A, IODUC of A alone would be incremented.
- While B is unloading both A's and B's IODUCs would be incremented
- While C is unloading both A's and C's IODUCs would be incremented, but **B's IODUC is not incremented**.

Yet, this does not match implementations, as observed through `document.open()`:

- Firefox increments all the parents' IODUCs for all three events
- Safari increments all parents' IODUCs for `pagehide` and `unload`; it does not increment any parents' IODUC for `beforeunload`
- (Chrome and Edge don't have an IODUC yet.)

A WPT-style test for this with the current spec as reference is available at https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt/blob/184c58a118733cf825393524bae3fb44bdd6a50d/html/webappapis/dynamic-markup-insertion/opening-the-input-stream/ignore-opens-during-unload.window.js#L35-L57. The `assert_equals(innerIframe.contentDocument.childNodes.length, 0);` line fails on Safari and Firefox for both `pagehide` and `unload`.

More realistically, I am implementing the counter in Chromium right now, and for implementation ease I'll probably follow Firefox and Safari on `pagehide` and `unload`, but the current spec on `beforeunload`.
